Each agent's own task.jsonl shows it died in under 1 second: session ended (other) without landing. This is a harness bug (label c), not the models or the guard: spike.jsonl shows these exact three model ids working fine through spike.mjs's own query() path at 04:30-04:33Z, minutes either side of these failures -- real edits landed, real OpenRouter cost billed. The only difference is the code path that spawns the agent (spawn_agent/Agents.js door() vs spike.mjs's direct query()). Found and fixed the real cause of the uniform rule-append FAIL across every model: the test's own prompt asked agents to append {"rule_test_append":{...}}, a key the task.jsonl schema (.claude/hooks/jsonl-schema.mjs) does not recognize as a verb, so append.mjs refuses it for every model -- label (c), a harness bug in my own test, not a model weakness. Confirmed by reading the agent log for the one run that stalled 3 minutes: it correctly ran append.mjs, got refused, then spent its whole turn trying to diagnose the refusal itself and ran out of time. Fixed rules.mjs's append test to use a real, already-registered verb ({"log":{"at":"NOW","msg":"...nonce=..."}}).

Also fixed rules.mjs's cost_usd, which read 0 for every OpenRouter run because it checked wait_for_agent's own cost figure before OpenRouter's real dollar amount settles. It now polls the spend guard's ledger (openrouter.jsonl) by agent id for the real, settled figure. Both fixes are in the qf-7 worktree now (not yet committed) since the parent asked for the fix to land there first, then merge into michael/dev alongside probes.mjs's own shared-helper exports.

Next: commit this fix in qf-7, merge michael/dev into qf-7 to pick up probes.mjs's shared exports, resolve rules.mjs keeping both sides, then rerun the full OpenRouter battery once more in the main tree (the previous append rows are invalid regardless of model, so a cost-only patch would not fix them) and send the final table.

Read both control agents' own logs. Real cause, different from the wrong-tree hypothesis: page-blog's agent never calls new-task at all (goes straight from the minion skill to new-page/page and does real, good work -- even a full merge.mjs smoke test -- without ever opening a task); log-line's agent DOES write a task.jsonl, but invents an ad hoc path inside its own scratch dir (.../probe/<run>/ai/task.jsonl, non-standard shape) because nothing tells it where a probe with no pre-existing brief should log to. Since the CONTROL fails both the same way, this is label (a) per probes.md's own rule, not (b) or (c) -- my wrong-tree fix is still correct and worth keeping (it would catch a model that opens the task in the right place but the wrong tree), it just was not the cause here.
